messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH p95 latency for /v1/generate in hosted-us-west-2 — p95=2.4s (baseline ~0.35s). Alert ID: AB-1767894321. Please acknowledge and create incident channel.
oncall-sam: acked. I'm on it — spinning up traces and checking node pools. Triage name: latency-rca-1767894321.
jin: seeing coincident perf counters spike on a subset of nodes that received kernel update yesterday (nodepool-kernel-2026-03-16). runqueue and context-switch increases on those hosts. link to rollout: https://infra.internal/rollouts/2026-03-16-kernel
maria: dropping a trace sample (shortened) — looks like a few spans spend long time in "sys_read" / "page_fault" then in runtime decode.
maria: TRACE: https://traces.internal/trace/1767894321/span
maria: span dump:
```
span: request.handler  total=2400ms
  span: model.decode    150ms
  span: kv_cache_lookup   5ms
  span: syscall.read   2000ms  <-- long tail
  span: runtime.blk_io   180ms
```
devon: quick customer check: ~0.6% of requests hit p95 spike, mostly long-prompts (>2048 tokens) and some streaming sessions. No widespread errors but UX impacted for a subset of commercial customers.
oncall-sam: running quick perf on an impacted pod (cmd):
```
kubectl -n runtime exec pod/runtime-xyz -- sh -c "perf stat -e context-switches,cpu-migrations,page-faults -p $(pidof runtime) sleep 10"
```
oncall-sam: sample perf stat output:
```
  2,380,012 context-switches
    12,345 cpu-migrations
  1,014,567 page-faults
```
jin: hypothesis 1: kernel preempt/config change on updated nodes is increasing blocking syscall tail (pagefault latency) under certain memory access patterns -> long syscall.sys_read spikes. hypothesis 2: KV cache miss pattern for long prefixes amplifies syscall IO (swap? network fs?). Need dmesg/syscalls and perf samples.
maria: I pulled dmesg from one impacted node — saw repeated softirqs and a few WARN_ONCE page_alloc failures (logs redacted):
```
[  123.456] softirq: 4567 blocked for 2000ms
[  124.001] WARNING: page_alloc failed, order:0, mode:0x20
```
ops-bot: nodepool autoscaler triggered replacements for ~8 nodes in us-west-2 yesterday as part of kernel rollout. affected subset: np-uw2-2026-03-16. Scaling events: 2026-03-16T03:12Z -> 2026-03-16T04:10Z.
devon: mitigation idea: shift traffic from updated nodepool to the dedicated fallback pool (dedicated-usw2-oldkernel) for heavy prompts + enable aggressive KV prefix caching for these routes. That should cut backend IO hits.
oncall-sam: implemented temporary route rule at 1767894380: routed /v1/generate for token_count>1024 to dedicated-usw2-oldkernel. Early numbers: p95 down to 0.42s for rerouted traffic (monitoring link: https://metrics.internal/d/latency/1767894321). :thumbsup:
jin: good. while mitigation is live, can someone collect full perf samples and run `perf record -F 99 -p <pid> -g -- sleep 30` so we can get flamegraphs? Also capture ` /proc/interrupts` and `vmstat` periodic snapshot.
maria: uploading logs and traces to trace-bucket: gs://incidents/1767894321/ (I dropped syscalls.log, dmesg.log, perf.data.zip). Please use `tracebridge` tool to stitch traces.
devon: assembling timeline for RCA doc:
  - 03:09Z alert fires (p95 2.4s)
  - 03:12Z identify correlation with nodepool-kernel-2026-03-16
  - 03:18Z route rule created to divert heavy prompts
  - 03:22Z observed p95 fall to 0.42s on diverted traffic
  - 03:40Z perf data uploaded
oncall-sam: next steps: (1) full flamegraph analysis (jin), (2) verify kernel config diff and escalation to infra (maria+jin), (3) postmortem + customer impact note (devon). I'll keep the mitigation for 4h or until infra patch rollback is scheduled.
jin: I'll take flamegraphs and kernel diff. If flamegraph implicates kernel syscall stall path we'll propose rollback of the kernel package for the affected nodepool. assigning to infra oncall if confirmed.
ops-bot: noted. created infra ticket INF-1767894321 and scheduled rollback window candidate 2026-03-17T06:00Z. infra-oncall pinged.
oncall-sam: thanks folks. Drop any additional log snippets in the bucket and I will update the timeline. Closing live coordination once rollback/patch plan confirmed. :white_check_mark:
